sub_graphs.title: EIP-2124: Fork Identifier Computation
sub_graphs.description: Models the computation of FORK_HASH and FORK_NEXT values that identify chain configuration

nodes.label: Node Initializing
nodes.description: Node is starting up and needs to compute its fork identifier

nodes.label: Load Genesis Hash
nodes.description: Retrieve the 32-byte genesis block hash

nodes.label: Collect Past Fork Blocks
nodes.description: Gather all fork block numbers that have already occurred (in ascending order)

nodes.label: Compute CRC32 Checksum
nodes.description: Calculate IEEE CRC32 over genesis hash and past fork block numbers (uint64 big-endian)

nodes.label: FORK_HASH Computed
nodes.description: 4-byte FORK_HASH value has been calculated

nodes.label: Determine Next Fork Block
nodes.description: Identify the next anticipated fork block number, or 0 if unknown

nodes.label: Fork ID Ready
nodes.description: Complete fork identifier (FORK_HASH, FORK_NEXT) is ready for use

sub_graphs.title: EIP-2124: Peer Compatibility Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the four validation rules for determining peer compatibility based on fork identifiers

nodes.label: Peer Fork ID Received
nodes.description: Remote peer's fork identifier has been received

nodes.label: Compare Fork Hashes
nodes.description: Compare local FORK_HASH with remote FORK_HASH

nodes.label: Fork Hash Matches
nodes.description: Local and remote FORK_HASH values are identical

nodes.label: Fork Hash Differs
nodes.description: Local and remote FORK_HASH values are different

nodes.label: Check Head Position
nodes.description: Check if remote's announced next fork has passed locally

nodes.label: Check Subset/Superset Relationship
nodes.description: Determine if remote is subset (behind) or superset (ahead) of local forks

nodes.label: Peer Accepted
nodes.description: Peer is compatible; connection should be maintained

nodes.label: Peer Rejected
nodes.description: Peer is incompatible; connection should be terminated

ambiguities.text: The specification states 'duplicate block numbers checksummed only once' but doesn't clarify how duplicates arise
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume duplicates could occur when multiple EIPs activate at the same block; each unique block number is included once in the checksum

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'remote is a superset of local past forks completable with known future forks' is complex
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this means the remote FORK_HASH can be reproduced by adding known upcoming forks to the local chain configuration

ambiguities.text: The specification doesn't detail how to handle forks that are announced but then postponed or cancelled
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume FORK_NEXT is updated when fork schedules change, and peers recalculate their fork ID accordingly

implicit_assumptions.description: Peers are assumed to report their fork ID honestly; there's no cryptographic proof
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious peers could lie about their fork ID to connect to incompatible nodes, wasting resources or enabling attacks

implicit_assumptions.description: CRC32 collisions are assumed to be sufficiently rare for practical use
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Different chain configurations could produce the same FORK_HASH, allowing incompatible peers to connect

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes have accurate knowledge of past and upcoming fork block numbers
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect fork configuration would lead to incorrect FORK_HASH and peer rejection from the network
